title: Pyramid 4.1 — precise progress and bounded context

intent.statement: Engineers can extend an existing plan, continue authorized independent work and reach a verified small outcome with less avoidable requalification and context overhead while preserving current evidence, authority, visual-review and history boundaries.

success_evidence.description: A new consumer preserves an unchanged prerequisite and its current producer proof; changed provider or composition claims still stale.
Task ownership renewal remains separate from reviewed procedure source and host authorization; stale authority is refused.
Agents distinguish authorization, review, task readiness, audit readiness and verification using a small STE-inspired operational profile.
Planning selects the first honest public journey, minimal nonduplicated harness and justified dependencies; blocked checks do not serialize independent authorized work.
Engineers inspect artifact footprint and source/generated/evidence classification without deletion, evidence laundering or unbounded normal context.
A 4.1 candidate is qualified on both hosts with current inherited regression evidence, bounded matched decision cases and honest usage/qualification limits.

constraints: Build on upstream 4.0.0 main at 3d787c5; support Codex and Claude with one base release.
Keep project format V3 and schema-1 history readable; preserve schema-2 proof and canonical atomicity/guards.
Use real subprocess/file/state observations for mechanisms; do not treat synthetic passed fixtures, hashes or screenshots as execution/visual judgment.
No new authority, extra routine human gate, hidden failed evidence, broad generated/evidence exclusions or normal-context history scans.
non_goals: Automatic compaction or host hooks; persistent scheduler/agent launcher; full STE compliance/dictionary/parser.
Automatic GC, evidence deletion, history compaction, Git LFS or Observer redesign.
Changing the two investigated projects, deploying Hemkar, publishing/pushing or installing 4.1 in this planning turn.

assumptions.statement: Selective instructions can reduce avoidable context and retries without a critical decision regression; effect size is unknown.
Current host capabilities can qualify candidate skills in isolated profiles without replacing user installations; blocked support remains a gate blocker.

evidence.claim: Source main and both installed hosts match upstream 3d787c5 (4.0.0); 112 plugin files match per host. The restored baseline passed 160 tests and repository validation.
replan_project compares all incident edges; contracts() includes all proof consumers. Consumer growth can change a producer's graph or proof identity.
evidence.freshness: Read upstream 4.0.0 on 2026-10-04; behavior reproduction belongs TASK-411

evidence.claim: Two active sessions exposed guard-literal requalification, excessive harness drift, useful real-DB/delta-review patterns and repeated policy checks; their risks and schemas differ.
evidence.freshness: Bounded October 4 observations; sanitized mechanism cases, not a causal productivity estimate

evidence.claim: STE and normative requirement wording motivate clearer conditions and terminology; token or outcome gains for coding hosts remain unproven.
evidence.freshness: Research reviewed 2026-10-04; test transfer in TASK-422

evidence.claim: 4.0 replan requires a complete candidate and performs stable-ID comparisons, but canonical snapshots and every task projection are rewritten. Targeted candidate assembly need not redraft unchanged tasks; write counts are not model token counts.
evidence.freshness: Source inspected and design direction approved 2026-10-04; optimization and benefit remain unimplemented/unmeasured

decisions.question: How should 4.1 reduce replan drafting and generated-file churn without weakening canonical safety?
decisions.choice: Assemble the complete candidate from the current plan using narrowly scoped stable-ID/field changes; preserve untouched content and skip writing generated projections whose bytes are unchanged. Keep full validation and guarded canonical publication.
alternatives: Redraft every task and evidence contract for each replan
Apply raw line-number edits to canonical JSON
Add a general patch API, new graph engine or incremental cache before demonstrating a need
decisions.rationale: The 4.0 runtime requires a complete candidate, compares node/edge changes, rewrites canonical snapshots and rebuilds all generated task projections. Full serialization does not require model redrafting. A copied candidate with targeted edits reduces avoidable authoring context; content-equality checks can reduce output writes without trusting stale caches. Preserve full validation, current guards/context, event/head integrity, dependency/proof invalidation and history. This records design direction only: bind concrete implementation scope and regression acceptance in a narrow plan update before implementing this slice. Measure actual decisions/usage and generated-write behavior; do not infer token savings from fewer disk writes.

decisions.question: What is the smallest useful 4.1 delivery ladder?
decisions.choice: First preserve exact producer claims, then verify bounded agent decisions, then qualify the joined candidate and read-only footprint reporting.
alternatives: One final gate after all cleanup and platform work
decisions.rationale: The current demonstrable baseline is a working 4.0.0 CLI with 160 tests and matching two-host installs, but consumer-growth false staleness and workflow ambiguity remain. I1 fixes a real public planning path; I2 resolves actual case decisions; I3 adds bounded footprint visibility and candidate qualification. Evidence is inherited at each gate. No setup-only rung or extra final intent gate is needed.

decisions.question: How much automation and language control belong in 4.1?
decisions.choice: Small original operational profile, semantic fixes and one optional read-only inspection mode; reuse current runtime, schemas and hosts.
alternatives: Full STE dictionary and stylistic compliance gate
Automated permissions, source qualification and compaction hooks
Automatic evidence cleanup and a benchmark service
decisions.rationale: The observed friction is incorrect coupling and repeated decisions, not missing another controller. Preserve human authority and machine-enforced evidence. Test outcome/usage effects rather than infer them from bytes.

nodes.title: Preserve unchanged producer claims when consumers grow
nodes.summary: Fix directional graph and schema-2 producer proof invalidation with actual positive/negative lifecycle regressions.

acceptance_criteria.description: A real disposable CLI/API reproduction shows the 4.0 consumer-growth failure before repair; schema-1 and schema-2 checks preserve an unchanged provider and current producer proof after the fix.
Changed provider contract/source/prerequisite, contribution membership, selection and inherited composition still stale the affected old/new claims; a new consumer is not automatically accepted.
Stored 4.0 observations/history remain untouched and honest under any documented compatibility rule; stale guards and failed/unknown proof still refuse acceptance.

verification.procedure: Reproduce consumer growth against the pinned 4.0 baseline in disposable projects, repair the semantic boundary, then run positive and negative graph/proof CLI scenarios with actual files, stored proofs, guards and event heads. Preserve the baseline failure; inspect actual transitions and unchanged history. Do not replace source coverage with status fixtures.

verification.environment: Disposable local projects and owned test processes; no production, personal credentials or existing installations. Record candidate, runtime, host/model identity when applicable. Failed/not-run observations remain visible.

deliverables: Fix directional graph and schema-2 producer proof invalidation with actual positive/negative lifecycle regressions.
non_goals: Do not weaken authorization, acceptance, proof freshness or independent review.
No broad refactor, implicit proof migration or automatic new-consumer acceptance.
